# Logical review of Pro's boundary-value proof

**Verdict: PASS conditional on the stated exact half-line operator and interval bounds.** The displayed argument is logically compatible with the original homogeneous mixed-tenure model. I found no contradiction in its inherited-state construction, injectivity argument, convergent-sequence proof, or fertility and population implications. The stationary derivative step needs the explicit tail-matrix argument given below; it follows from the stated structure and bounds.

This is **not numerical reproduction**. I read only the preserved response at /Users/tommasodesanto/Desktop/Projects/Fertility/Fertility_Spring26/output/model/simplified_olg_amendments/oracle_transition_math_response.md. The advertised coefficient file and executable verifier were not yet available when this logical review began. Their numerical claims, including the enlarged reform rectangle, remain unverified here. The only computation I ran checks exact arithmetic consequences of the stated bounds.

## 1. Actual initial old

The inherited vector
\[
I=(Y_0,O_0,p^-,a_O^-,H_O^-,a_R^-)
\]
is sufficient for this homogeneous example because conditional original policies do not vary with the realized ownership taste. It represents two conditional old states and their masses, rather than replacing a heterogeneous distribution by its mean.

The proposed initial formulas are correct:
\[
M_0=\frac{\gamma}{1+\gamma+\omega_B}
O_0p^-(a_O^-+P_0H_O^-+T_0),\qquad
R_0=aO_0(1-p^-).
\]
They use original purchased title \(H_O^-\), revalued at the new current price. Financial claims remain fixed and include repayment of the mortgage originated under the baseline:
\[
a_O^-=
\frac{a_{t_p-1}^{\prime,B}
-\phi_0P_{t_p-1}^Bh_{t_p-1}^{O,B}}q.
\]
Thus the new financed share does not alter existing debt. The per-renter financial state must likewise come from actual earlier saving.

The comparison has to be interpreted as two unexpected announcements before the relevant date's choices. Earlier saving, ownership, purchases, and rental entry use baseline forecasts, including at \(t_p-1\). One must not impose the pre-announcement deterministic rental-entry identity with the unexpectedly changed realized price at \(t_p\). The response explicitly maintains this forecast distinction.

The numerical part must still prove that every baseline-generated conditional old state lies in the displayed inherited box and that each original old problem remains feasible on that box. Its claim is stronger than a check of \(M_0\) or of aggregate resources alone. The displayed formulation is correct conditional on those verifications.

## 2. Why the preconditioner is injective

The right-product bound is the relevant one:
\[
\|I-\mathcal L A\|<1.
\]
For any bounded residual sequence \(z\) with \(Az=0\),
\[
z=(I-\mathcal L A)z,\qquad
\|z\|\le\|I-\mathcal L A\|\,\|z\|,
\]
which implies \(z=0\). Therefore \(A\) is injective. Since the original residual is bounded throughout the verified box, \(A\mathcal F(X)=0\) then implies \(\mathcal F(X)=0\). Fixed points of \(X-A\mathcal F(X)\) are genuine equilibria.

The left-product bound \(\|I-A\mathcal L\|<1\) alone would not establish injectivity of \(A\) in an infinite-dimensional space. The response correctly retains both products. They must be verified as operators on the infinite half-line, not only on a finite matrix truncation.

## 3. Existence and convergence of the complete infinite sequence

Take the componentwise supremum norm,
\[
\|X\|_\infty=\sup_{t\ge0}\max(|P_t|,|Y_{t+1}|).
\]
Conditional on the uniform derivative bound, the mean-value inequality gives a contraction constant at most \(1/20\) on the convex verified box. Exact anchor equilibrium and the parameter-forcing bounds imply the two self-map inequalities. Their exact positive slacks are
\[
R_B-\frac{10/3}{20000}-\frac{R_B}{20}
=\frac7{300000},
\]
\[
R_P-\frac{451/100}{20000}-\frac{R_P}{20}
=\frac3{250000},\qquad
R-R_B-R_P=\frac1{20000}.
\]
The later construction is centered on the actual baseline tail. Its residual at zero policy change is zero with the same inherited data. Consequently the bounds can be uniform in \(t_p\), provided the stated inherited-box inclusion is verified.

Convergent two-component sequences form a closed subspace \(c\) of \(\ell^\infty\). The original residual maps \(c\) to \(c\): after finitely many initial rows, its arguments are finitely many shifts of \(X\), its parameters are constant, and its formulas are continuous on the verified positive domain. A finite-band operator with a time-homogeneous tail also maps \(c\) to \(c\). Thus \(\mathcal T=X-A\mathcal F(X)\) preserves \(c\).

Starting the baseline iteration at the constant reference sequence and the policy iteration at the convergent baseline tail therefore gives convergent fixed points, since convergence in the supremum norm preserves membership in \(c\). Because \(A\) is injective, the full equilibrium residual vanishes. Taking its tail limit proves that the limiting point is a stationary equilibrium.

The finite-window exponential argument is also correct, with the following indexing detail. For \(X_t=(P_t,Y_{t+1})\), the original residual's homogeneous tail uses offsets \(-3,\ldots,+2\). The \(-3\) term comes from \(T_{t-1}\) in the preceding young cohort's resources. The first three residual rows are exceptional. With \(A\)'s tail offsets \(-24,\ldots,+24\), the homogeneous part of \(\mathcal T\) begins at row 27 and uses \(X_{t-27},\ldots,X_{t+26}\).

For \(t\ge27\), the constant stationary limit is a fixed point of that tail row even though it need not satisfy the actual initial-old boundary. Rowwise contraction then gives
\[
E_j\le\frac1{20}E_{j-27},\qquad
E_0\le2R=\frac1{1000},
\]
and hence exactly the displayed exponential bound. This proves the complete tail; it is not a finite terminal condition.

## 4. Stationary derivatives: the needed tail-matrix step

The full half-line operator generally does **not** map constant sequences to constant sequences at its boundary. The stationary argument should therefore be stated using its tail limit.

Let \(A_k\), \(k=-24,\ldots,24\), be the homogeneous tail blocks, and define
\[
A_\infty=\sum_{k=-24}^{24}A_k.
\]
Let \(f(x;\lambda)\) be the two-dimensional stationary residual obtained by assigning the same \(x=(P,Y)\) to every argument of the original homogeneous residual. Its Jacobian is the sum of all six dated derivative blocks. On constant inputs, the tail derivative of \(\mathcal T\) is
\[
K_\infty=I_2-A_\infty D_xf.
\]
The asserted infinite-operator bound implies
\[
\|K_\infty\|_\infty\le1/20.
\]
Thus the square product \(A_\infty D_xf\) is invertible; both \(A_\infty\) and \(D_xf\) are invertible. The finite-dimensional implicit-function theorem gives the stationary derivative directly. It satisfies
\[
w_\lambda^*=K_\infty w_\lambda^*
+c_{\lambda,\infty},\qquad
c_{\lambda,\infty}=-A_\infty f_\lambda.
\]
This is the justified meaning of the response's statement about taking constant sequences. No interchange of differentiation and an infinite-time limit is needed.

The coefficient audit must supply \(A_\infty\), the stationary residual derivative, and the stated stationary-tail forcing bounds, or verify their exact implication from the tail stencil. Injectivity of the full half-line \(A\) alone should not substitute for this finite-dimensional argument.

## 5. Signs and their scope

The first-row error bound and the global derivative-norm bound give the following exact conditional lower bounds:
\[
\partial_\vartheta Y_1>
\frac{46223}{28500}>\frac85,\qquad
\partial_\phi Y_1>
\frac{951}{23750}>\frac1{25}.
\]
The stationary-tail bounds and the full contraction constant give
\[
\partial_\vartheta Y^*>
\frac{12509}{5700}>2,\qquad
\partial_\phi Y^*>
\frac{81}{95}>\frac45.
\]
I independently checked this arithmetic with fractions. In particular the final credit-impact margin above \(1/25\) is only \(1/23750\); the advertised interval bounds must be verified exactly rather than rounded.

The conditional resource and choice formulas are smooth on the strictly feasible box. The uniform contraction therefore supports differentiating the infinite fixed point with inherited data held fixed. Integrating the positive theta derivative downward lowers baseline initial fertility and terminal population; integrating the positive phi derivative upward raises policy-date fertility and terminal population relative to the same continuing baseline.

At either announcement, \(Y_0\) is fixed, so \(\bar n_0=Y_1/(\nu Y_0)\) preserves the impact sign. Positive stationary demography implies \(Y^*=O^*\), so \(N^*=2Y^*\) preserves the terminal sign.

The cumulative identity also follows from the original cohort law. Common initial young masses make the finite log fertility ratios telescope into the log relative young population. Exponential convergence and positivity make the log series absolutely summable. Since stationary adult population is twice young population,
\[
\sum_{t=t_p}^\infty\log\frac{\bar n_t^1}{\bar n_t^B}
=\log\frac{N_1^*}{N_B^*}>0.
\]
This implies neither an all-date fertility ordering nor a welfare gain. The policy need not raise fertility above replacement or restore the original population level.

## Objects still required for numerical acceptance

These are verification requirements, not inferred failures of the verifier. After this logical review was completed, the lead reported that the code had been retrieved and that it checks both inverse products through 56 block rows and nonlinear bounds through rows 0–28. The lead also reported that forcing row 28 touches only residual rows 4 and above. Those reported supports exceed the boundary coverage required below and permit the homogeneous-tail interpretation. I did not inspect or replay the newly retrieved code; numerical acceptance remains a separate review.

1. The exact dyadic coefficient file for \(A\), with coordinate ordering, norm, boundary-row indexing, and complete tail stencil specified.
2. The exact original anchor linearization \(\mathcal L\), including initial rows 0, 1, and 2. Both product bounds must check rows 0–26 individually and the homogeneous tail from row 27, assuming the advertised stencil support. Checking only the first 24 exceptional rows of \(A\) would not suffice for the products.
3. Exact anchor equilibrium or a separately accounted residual error; fixed original taste parameters; and rigorous nonlinear derivative/forcing bounds throughout the entire price/population, parameter, and inherited-state boxes.
4. Original individual household margin checks, including actual initial owners and renters, plus an explicit inclusion proof for every inherited state generated by a baseline in radius \(R_B\). Earlier mortgages, titles, and baseline forecasts must be retained.
5. The tail matrix \(A_\infty\), stationary derivative/forcing checks described above, and exact outward endpoints supporting all four derivative signs.
6. A reproducible full-half-line certificate receipt tied to the actual source and coefficients. A successful finite inverse, terminally closed simulation, or browser claim of a verifier run is not a substitute.

No repository or main-note file was changed. No claimed Pro coefficient bound, nonlinear enclosure, or household interval was replayed in this review. The conclusion is a logical conditional pass, preserved separately from the lead's pending numerical reproduction.

# Independent review of the Pro finite mixed-transition certificate

**PASS within the assigned arithmetic and infinite-operator scope.** No additional mathematical assumption or numerical certificate is needed for acceptance. The stationary argument should explicitly use the summed tail matrix, as stated below; applying the full half-line operator to a constant sequence would be incorrect at its boundary. This clarification supplies the intended argument without changing any bound or model equation.

Reviewed read-only: `/tmp/simplified_olg_pro_certificate/verify_finite_mixed_transition.py`, its exact dyadic coefficient JSON, and `output/model/simplified_olg_amendments/oracle_transition_math_response.md`. This review did not alter or rerun the executable's output-writing entry point. The lead separately owns the full verifier replay and identification with the original household problems.

## Arithmetic and derivatives

The interval arithmetic at verifier lines 96–160 encloses the represented real operations. Addition, multiplication, reciprocals and integer powers round outward to dyadics with denominator \(2^{90}\); the reciprocal requires a strictly signed denominator interval. The square-root endpoints use the exact integer square root of \(\lfloor x2^{180}\rfloor\). The logarithm uses \(z=(x-1)/(x+1)\) and bounds the omitted series after \(N\) terms by
\[
\frac{2|z|^{2N+1}}{(2N+1)(1-z^2)}.
\]
The exponential uses a Taylor polynomial of degree 33 and remainder at most \(3|x|^{34}/34!\) under the asserted \(|x|<1\). Monotonicity justifies endpoint evaluation. None of the accepted inequalities uses floating-point arithmetic; the floating conversion in `__repr__` is diagnostic only.

The fertility formula and its derivatives at lines 194–206 are consistent with the implicit first-order condition. Writing \(B=\rho x+\chi n\) and \(s=h-\kappa n\), multiplication of that condition gives
\[
\chi\kappa(\vartheta+\rho+\alpha)n^2
-\{\kappa B(\vartheta+\alpha)+\chi h(\vartheta+\rho)\}n
+\vartheta Bh=0.
\]
The code selects the stable expression for the smaller root and verifies \(n,x,s>0\). On this domain the original first-order condition is strictly decreasing in \(n\), so that root is the unique feasible solution. Its denominator
\[
\vartheta/n^2+\alpha\kappa^2/s^2+\chi^2/(\rho x^2)
\]
and the three numerator terms for changes in \(\vartheta,h,B\) have the correct signs and factors. The centered value difference at lines 210–214 includes the necessary \((\vartheta-\vartheta_0)\log(n_0^O/n_0^R)\) term. Its envelope derivative includes the renter's future rent. The logistic derivative is \(\pi(1-\pi)/\sigma_\xi\) times that value derivative. Interval dependency can widen these enclosures but cannot invalidate them.

## The half-line and its initial rows

The equilibrium residual has block offsets \(-3,\ldots,2\). Date 0 uses the separate actual-old boundary. Dates 1 and 2 still depend on fixed inherited population entries. Date 3 is the first fully homogeneous row. I independently checked every coordinate in the union of the interval and exact derivative supports at dates 0–2, including coordinates absent from one representation. The exact derivative lies inside every corresponding interval.

I also checked that residual values and **all** coordinate and parameter derivative intervals at dates 3, 4, 27 and 100 agree exactly after translating coordinate indices. Thus `min(t,3)` in `derivative_bounds` correctly represents every residual row.

The first 24 preconditioner block rows are exceptional. The allowed tail support is \([-24,24]\); the supplied coefficients actually use \([-24,22]\), so the stated support is conservative. In \(A\mathcal L\), every residual row reached from output date \(t\ge27\) has date at least 3. In \(\mathcal LA\), every preconditioner row reached from \(t\ge27\) has date at least 24. Consequently both products are homogeneous from date 27 onward. All dates 0–26 must be checked; date 26 really differs from the tail in several components.

The product calculation at lines 278–292 includes dates 0–55 and composes complete sparse rows, without truncating output columns. I independently confirmed exact translation of both products at dates 27, 28, 55, 56, 100 and 1000. The nonlinear and forcing loop covers dates 0–28, hence all exceptional dates and the homogeneous tail. Its row bound is the valid inequality
\[
\|(I-A D\mathcal F)_{i,\cdot}\|_1
\le \|(I-A\mathcal L)_{i,\cdot}\|_1
+\sum_j|A_{ij}|\|(D\mathcal F-\mathcal L)_{j,\cdot}\|_1.
\]
The two independently reproduced half-line defects are approximately \(1.73410244\,10^{-9}\) and \(2.77814412\,10^{-9}\), with \(\|A\|=4.009664285\) to the displayed precision. Acceptance uses their exact rational values.

## Stationary endpoint and infinite convergence

Define \(A_\infty=\sum_r A_r\), summing the two-by-two homogeneous tail coefficients, and define \(\mathcal L_\infty\) by summing the homogeneous residual coefficients. Independently obtained:
\[
A_\infty=\begin{pmatrix}
-261565807425/70368744177664 & 13764628571401/8796093022208\\
70282746471833/70368744177664 & 21635151094413/17592186044416
\end{pmatrix},
\]
\[
\det A_\infty=
-1940490816090222688503112591/1237940039285380274899124224\ne0.
\]
The exact defects of \(A_\infty\mathcal L_\infty\) and \(\mathcal L_\infty A_\infty\) are bounded by the respective full half-line defects. Restricting a **homogeneous tail row** to constant perturbations similarly gives
\(\|I-A_\infty D\mathcal F_\infty\|<1/20\), together with the advertised tail forcing bounds. This proves stationary invertibility and the stationary derivative estimates directly; differentiating a limiting infinite path is unnecessary.

The convergence proof in the response is valid. Finite-band operators with a homogeneous tail preserve convergent sequences. The baseline iteration starts from a constant sequence, and the policy iteration starts from the convergent baseline tail; uniform limits remain convergent. Passing the original residual to the limit gives \(\mathcal F_\infty(X^*)=0\). Comparison with that constant endpoint is valid in every homogeneous output row, giving \(E_j\le E_{j-27}/20\). The initial bound \(E_0\le2R=1/1000\) gives the reported complete exponential tail. No terminal condition or finite-horizon approximation is being used.

## Uniform bounds and finite changes

The entire derivative and forcing box includes the explicit inherited-state box. Generator bounds use baseline forecasts and net assets, and the policy parameter derivative holds those inherited entries fixed. The baseline and policy self-map inequalities have exact positive slack, respectively \(7/300000\) and \(3/250000\); the common-box slack is \(1/20000\). They therefore give complete infinite fixed points for every admitted shock and every intervention date. Smooth finite formulas on the uniformly strict domain provide the required Fréchet differentiability on the sequence space.

The four signed lower bounds following from the forcing and contraction estimates are, exactly,
\[
\partial_\vartheta Y_1>46223/28500>8/5,\qquad
\partial_\phi Y_1>951/23750>1/25,
\]
\[
\partial_\vartheta Y^*>12509/5700>2,\qquad
\partial_\phi Y^*>81/95>4/5.
\]
The implementation asserts these signs using rational arithmetic. Integrating the first two with the appropriate inherited data fixed, and the last two in the stationary system, is justified throughout the certified parameter intervals.

**Remaining condition for acceptance:** none within this audit's scope. Replace the response's shorthand “Taking constant sequences” with the explicit summed-tail construction above. Original-model equivalence and household optimality remain the lead's separate checks, rather than conclusions inferred merely from a passing numerical verifier.
